Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst possible single operation occurs when a vertex has an edge to every other vertex in the graph, giving it a cost of |V| − 1. In a simple directed graph, no vertex can have more than |V| − 1 outgoing edges, so this bound on the out-degree of any single vertex is tight and represents the maximum cost of one operation in the sequence.

* The total cost of the entire sequence of |V| operations equals |E|, since Σᵥ d⁺(v) = |E| (each directed edge is counted exactly once in the out-degree of its tail vertex).
* By aggregate analysis, the average amortized cost per operation is the total cost divided by the number of operations, which gives **|E| / |V|**.

In summary, the worst-case single operation costs O(|V|), while the amortized cost per operation under aggregate analysis is simply the average out-degree of the vertices.
